sections.$comment: `status` declares the full three-value enum itself; the contract's `valid_values` is derived from that, not the other way round. Until 2026-07-29 execute_modify collapsed "paused" to "inactive" on write, so a user's "paused" survived only until the next AI edit; see docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-wave-5-storage-keys-reference.md 1.1.1. `references` is a child list whose rows store `name`, NOT the `ref_name` the entity declares as its identifier -- server.write_entity.

sections.title: Interests
sections.description: What you love, and what you are curious about

info.overview: Things you're into, tagged as a passion (what you love doing or following) or a curiosity (what you want to explore). AI uses this to understand your motivations and tailor suggestions.
tips: Passion: something you care deeply about that drives you, such as sustainability, design, storytelling, education, technology.
Curiosity: something you want to explore or learn more about but haven't dived into yet, such as quantum computing, fermentation, urban planning, linguistics.
No pressure on curiosities: these can be fleeting interests or serious research areas.

element.description: Things you're into: kind=passion for what you love doing/following, kind=curiosity for what you want to explore

sections.$comment: The entity's `day_type` is a ROUTER selecting which sub-object to write, never itself stored, so it is deliberately not bound. The two day keys are fixed and execute_modify's sleep branch rejects any other -- which is also why sleep is one of the few entities still written by a branch of its own rather than by server.write_entity: its rows are two sibling objects chosen by a parameter, not one array.
